Diplomacy colours: toggle button: colour players by diplomatic stance (ally, enemy, neutral) instead of their own colours
Idle workers: accessible name of the minimap button that selects the next idle worker; it also shows how many there are
Perspective: accessible name of the list choosing whose view of the match to show (observer or a player)
Sound off: button label while sound is off; pressing it turns sound on
Master: label of the master volume slider
Effects: label of the sound effects volume slider
Match time: accessible name of the match clock
Minimap: accessible name of the minimap canvas; also the label of the folded minimap tab
Follow with the camera: accessible name of the portrait button that moves the camera to the selected unit
Frames per second: accessible name of the frame rate readout
Network statistics: accessible name of a debug panel
Profiling statistics: accessible name of a debug panel
Memory and storage statistics: accessible name of a debug panel
Playback speed: accessible name of the replay speed list
Timeline: accessible name of the replay slider
Live: button that jumps playback to the live edge of the match
Current match: button that returns from a replay, or from a stored match opened by its link, to the match in progress
Copy link: button that copies a link to the match at the moment playback is at
Link copied: label the same button shows for 2 seconds after copying the link
Benchmark: button that runs a graphics benchmark
Download report: link that saves the benchmark report file
Frame stats: checkbox label: show the frame rate counter
Material maps: label of a list: surface detail maps on or off
Triplanar cliffs: label: a cliff texturing technique, technical term
Scene: settings group heading for sky, fog and particles
Flat world: label: Easter egg option, draws elephants holding up the map from below, as in the flat earth myth
Projectiles: label: arrows and other projectiles shown or hidden
Status bars: settings group heading for the bars (health, capture) drawn over units and buildings
Show all status bars: label of an on/off list: draw the health and capture bars of every unit and building on screen, not only the selected ones
Range overlays: settings group heading for the range circles drawn around selected buildings
Attack ranges (Alt+C): label of a list; the key combination in brackets stays as is
Aura ranges (Alt+V): label of a list; the key combination in brackets stays as is
Heal ranges (Alt+B): label of a list; the key combination in brackets stays as is
Silhouettes: settings group heading for the unit silhouettes option
Unit silhouettes (Alt+Shift+S): label of an on/off list: draw units hidden behind buildings, trees or hills as flat shapes in their player colour; the key combination in brackets stays as is
Bloom: label: glow effect around bright areas, technical term
Depth of field: label: camera blur effect for distant objects, technical term
Assets for the 3D view: heading of a dialog about downloading and storing game files in the browser
To show the match in 3D, this observer u: first paragraph of the storage dialog: what is downloaded and why
Over time this observer may store up to: paragraph of the storage dialog; keep {size} unchanged, it is replaced with a size such as 4.2 GB
You don't need to wait for any of it. Th: paragraph of the storage dialog: the match starts right away
To load fast on any device, the graphics: paragraph of the storage dialog: graphics start at minimum quality and can be changed in the settings
<b>Warm up</b> downloads, in the backgro: paragraph of the storage dialog explaining the Warm up button; keep the <b> tags, and translate the bold word as the Warm up button is translated
Press <b>F4</b>, or tap with four finger: paragraph of the storage dialog: how to show the debug panels; keep F4 unchanged
You can delete the stored files at any t: last paragraph of the storage dialog
Warm up now: button in the storage dialog that starts the background download
Got it: button that closes the storage dialog
Fold the queue: accessible name of a button that collapses the production queue panel
Unfold the queue: accessible name of a button that expands the production queue panel
Fold the orders panel: accessible name of a button that collapses the orders panel (stance, formation, alert, barter, garrison)
Unfold the orders panel: accessible name of a button that expands the orders panel (stance, formation, alert, barter, garrison)
Fold the build panel: accessible name of a button that collapses the panel of items to train, build, research or upgrade
Unfold the build panel: accessible name of a button that expands the panel of items to train, build, research or upgrade
Fold the details: accessible name of a button that collapses the selection details panel
Unfold the details: accessible name of a button that expands the selection details panel
Fold the top panel: accessible name of a button that collapses the top bar of resources and players
Unfold the top panel: accessible name of a button that expands the top bar of resources and players
Fold the minimap: accessible name of a button that collapses the minimap
Unfold the minimap: accessible name of a button that expands the minimap
Details: label of the folded details panel tab
Orders: label of the folded orders tab on phones: stance, formation, alert, barter and garrison buttons; keep it short, the tab is narrow
Build: label of the folded build tab on phones: buttons to train, build, research, upgrade, pack and lock gates; keep it short, the tab is narrow
Queue: label of the folded production queue tab on phones; keep it short, the tab is narrow
Sound on: button label while sound is on; pressing it turns sound off
Play: button that resumes a paused replay
Stop benchmark: button label while a benchmark runs
Downloading %(done)s MB: small corner indicator while 3D model files download over the network; the value is a number of megabytes
Warming up %(done)s / %(total)s MB: progress text of a button; the two values are numbers of megabytes
Warmed up: button label after the background download finished
Warm up: button that downloads every game file the match may need in advance
Warm up (%(failed)s failed): button label; the value is a number of files that failed; pressing retries
Match over: status text when the match ended
Match over. Next match in %(time)s: status text; the value is a countdown such as 0:42
New match: button on the player's page once their game has ended: opens the page that sets up a new game against the computer
Rematch: button on the player's page once their game has ended: starts a game again at once, with the same map, civilisations and opponents
Live stream starts in %(time)s: status text while the delayed broadcast has not started yet; the value is a countdown such as 1:42
on a match the server hosts: it stops every match after a fixed wall time or game time, and warns 15, 5 and 1 minute before; the value is a countdown such as 4:59
Default (browser: %(name)s): first entry of the language list; the value is the language name the browser asks for
warming up: benchmark phase, lower case, used inside a status line
measuring: benchmark phase, lower case, used inside a status line
Run %(index)s/%(total)s, %(phase)s: %(na: benchmark status line: run number, total, phase word, name of the setting tested
%(done)s of %(total)s runs measured, sto: benchmark result summary when stopped early
New game: heading and title of the page that opens a new match's setup, and its button; the setup page shares the heading
on the game setup page: another game the server hosts is running
Watch it: link from the game setup page to watch the game in progress
Back to your game: link from the game setup page back to the visitor's own game in progress
The server is shutting down. No new game: on the game setup page: the server was asked to stop and waits for the running games to finish before it exits
Players: game setup: label of the list choosing how many players the game has
You: game setup: the visitor plays this slot
Cannot start the game: %(error)s: game setup error; %(error)s is the server's reason, in English
View summary: button of the defeat or victory popup that opens the match summary
Continue watching: button of the defeat popup that closes it, after which the player goes on watching the match as an observer
Last recorded scores: heading of the match summary when the game stopped before the final scores were taken; the numbers are the last ones recorded
Chart type: label of a list in the match summary's charts that chooses which part of a value to draw (for example trained, killed or lost)
Nickname: label of the setup page's field for the name the visitor plays under; kept for the next game
3 to 20 letters, digits, dots, hyphens o: tooltip of the setup page's nickname field: the vanilla lobby's rule for a name
Join: button on a match's setup page that joins the match under the typed nickname
Take slot: button on an empty player slot of a match's setup page; the visitor sits in that slot
Step down: button on a match's setup page: the visitor gives up their player slot and becomes a spectator
Unseat: host's button on a match's setup page: removes another person from their player slot, making them a spectator
Seat: placeholder of the host's list that puts a spectator into a player slot of the match's setup page
Spectators: heading of the list of visitors without a player slot on a match's setup page
Host: tag next to the name of the person who controls the match's setup
This setup closes in %(time)s unless it: countdown on a match's setup page; %(time)s is minutes and seconds such as 9:41
heading shown when a match's setup page is no longer open
reason a setup closed: the host did not start the game in time
reason a setup closed: no visitor stayed
reason a setup closed: the server is stopping
reason a setup closed: its host started a different new game
notice on a match's setup page while the connection to the server is retried
the game is starting: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the game is already starting
only the host can start the game: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'
no player is seated: reason the game cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:' and as a hint on the Start button; no human holds a player slot
not every player is ready: reason the game cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:' and as a hint on the Start button
the settings cannot start a game: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the chosen settings are unusable
the setup is closed: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the setup closed meanwhile
the server is stopping: reason a game or setup cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the server is shutting down
cannot open the feed socket: reason a game or setup cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; an internal server error (the channel the game engine reports through)
the settings name no map: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; no map is chosen
cannot write the settings file: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; an internal server error
no such setup: reason the Start button was refused, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the game being set up no longer exists
not hosting: reason a game cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; this server only broadcasts games and hosts none
every match slot is in use: reason a new game cannot open, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the server already runs as many games as it can
cannot open a setup: reason a new game cannot open, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; an internal server error
bad nickname: reason a new game cannot open, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the typed nickname breaks the naming rule
no visitor cookie: reason a new game cannot open, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; the browser sent no cookie, for example because cookies are blocked
not in play mode: reason a game cannot start, shown after 'Cannot start the game:'; this server only broadcasts games and hosts none
Pause time left: header of the list of each player's remaining pause budget on the pause veil; each player may pause the game for 5 minutes in total
%(player)s: %(time)s: one line of that list; %(player)s is a player name, %(time)s minutes and seconds such as 4:59
%(player)s (disconnected): %(time)s: the same for a player who lost their connection; their absence pauses the game at their cost, unless every connected player also holds a pause
%(player)s is out of pause time; their p: countdown on the pause veil; %(time)s is like 0:05
the veil line under the pause time list while every connected player holds a pause; disconnected players do not break it, and no player's pause time runs down then
Pause time left: %(time)s: second line of the Menu's Pause button tooltip
the same tooltip when the player's 5 minute pause budget is spent and the button is disabled
Claim victory: button in the Menu, and the title of the claim question: the visitor claims the victory the seats that have left leave them
End game: Menu button that ends the game for every player; enabled for the host only
Kick: button on a player's row in the diplomacy window: the host removes that human player from the game
Kicked: tooltip of a Kick button for a player the host has already kicked
Wait: button of the claim offer popup: closes it without claiming
tooltip of a disabled Kick button: the player was defeated or resigned
tooltip of the disabled End game button for a player who is not the host
The host can end the game only in its fi: tooltip of the disabled End game button for the host
Available once every player still connec: tooltip of the disabled Claim victory button
Are you sure you want to end the game fo: question before End game; Yes ends the game for everyone
Claim victory? %(players)s will be resig: question before Claim victory; %(players)s is a list of player names, such as Alice, Bob
%(players)s left the game. Do you want t: popup offering Claim victory once the others have left; %(players)s is a list of player names
Kick %(player)s? They cannot play this m: question before a kick; %(player)s is the player's name
Hide observer chat: settings checkbox label in the Chat tab: a player does not see what observers write in chat
Hide what observers write while you play: tooltip of the Hide observer chat checkbox
too many messages: chat refusal shown to the sender: they sent messages too fast and must wait
message too long: chat refusal shown to the sender: the text is longer than the limit
empty message: chat refusal shown to the sender: the message has no text
observers cannot use that channel: chat refusal shown to an observer who picked Allies or Enemies, which only players can use
observers cannot message players: chat refusal shown to an observer who tried a private message to a player
only Everyone in setup: chat refusal in the game setup: only the Everyone addressee exists there; Everyone is the engine's name of the addressee that reaches all
no such member: chat refusal: the private message's addressee is not in the match
no addressee: chat refusal: a private message was sent without choosing whom to send it to
join first: chat refusal: the visitor must enter a nickname before sending
the chat is closed: chat refusal: the match has ended, so the chat takes no more messages
invalid nickname: chat refusal: the nickname stored in this browser breaks the nickname rule, so the visitor cannot chat
Ban: button that bans a player or observer from the match; it appears next to Kick in the diplomacy window and on the setup page's member rows
Banned: tooltip of a Ban button for a player who is already banned
Join again: button on a setup page after a kick: it reloads the page so the visitor can rejoin
message on a setup page after the host kicked this visitor out of it
message on a setup page for a visitor the host banned from the match
Ban %(name)s from this match? They canno: question before banning a member on the setup page; %(name)s is the member's name
Ban %(player)s? They cannot play or chat: question before banning a player in the diplomacy window; %(player)s is the player's name
Ban %(player)s from this match's chat?: question before the host bans an observer from the chat; %(player)s is the observer's name
Reserved for %(name)s: a setup slot a rematch keeps for an old player who has not joined yet; %(name)s is their name
waiting for the players of the last game: reason Start is disabled in a setup opened by a rematch while an old player's slot is still reserved
Join rematch: button on a player's end screen that opens the rematch setup the host opened
Lobby: button on a player's end screen that goes to the lobby page
you are banned from this match: server refusal shown when a banned visitor tries to join, chat or change a setup
that slot is reserved: server refusal shown when a visitor takes a slot a rematch holds for an old player
the time limit is reached: server refusal shown when a player tries to pause a match after its time limit ended it
Open setups: heading on the lobby page of the list of matches whose host has not started them yet
Running matches: heading on the lobby page of the list of matches being played now
Replays: heading on the lobby page of the list of finished, stored matches that can be watched again
Show more: button under the lobby page's replay list that lists older replays
lobby page text where the list of open setups is empty
lobby page text where the list of running matches is empty
lobby page text where the list of replays is empty
Setup: badge on a lobby card of a match that is still being set up by its host
Running: badge on a lobby card of a match that is being played
Replay: badge on a lobby card of a finished, stored match
Unknown map: lobby card text where the map's name is not known, as for an old stored match
Players:: label before the list of player names on a lobby card, each followed by the civ in brackets
Map: %(name)s: lobby card line; %(name)s is the map's name
Host: %(name)s: lobby card line; %(name)s is the nickname of the player who created the match
Seated: %(seated)s of %(max)s: lobby card line of an open setup: how many of its player slots hold a human, of all slots
Time: %(time)s: lobby card line of a running match; %(time)s is the game time played, as 12:34
Length: %(time)s: lobby card line of a replay; %(time)s is the match's length, as 12:34
Observers: %(count)s: lobby card line of a running match; %(count)s is how many viewers are watching it
Watch: button on a lobby card that opens a running match or a replay
